security_problem: Round-7 Codex P1: the stdio invocation digest is built by concatenating executable bytes and each literal argv value with NUL separator bytes. The serialization is not injective: executable X with args ["--safe"] hashes identically to a different executable whose content is X + NUL + "--safe" with no args; args ["a","b"] hash identically to a single arg "a\x00b"; and identical bytes can be interpreted interchangeably as executable content or argument content. An attacker who controls the on-disk artifact (or a confusing policy author) can therefore construct a different invocation that satisfies a pin on the intended one.
required_behavior: The stdio invocation digest is computed over a versioned, injectively framed serialization (kind stdio_invocation_sha256_v1): each component carries a domain tag, a fixed-width big-endian index (ordinal position for argv, declared arg position for entry payloads), an explicit byte length, and the exact bytes; the serialization is prefixed by a format-marker field. Different component structures never serialize to the same hash input: executable+argv differs from an executable embedding the same bytes; [a b] differs from [a\x00b]; reordered args differ; identical bytes in the executable-content domain vs the argument domain differ; identical payload files at different declared entry positions differ; payload mutation changes the digest; and resolution is deterministic across repeats. The policy loader accepts exactly one attestation kind (stdio_invocation_sha256_v1) and rejects unknown and legacy scheme names. The executable field streams bytes under the length declared by the same Stat that validated the artifact, and a size change between Stat and read fails closed. All prior round-1 through round-6 behavior is preserved: immutable launch identity, restart-bound replacement/introduction, changed-shape fail closed, normalized-order compatibility, single-snapshot launch shape, no-attestation zero resolver work, approval allow/signing-failure snapshots, all 11 canonical registry-runner rejects, undeclared runtime files never hashed, entry-artifact-not-transitive boundary, no argument leak on identity denial, and confused-deputy demo behavior.
failure_behavior: Fail closed for tools/call when the framed serialization is not injective (never allow a different invocation structure to satisfy a pin); reject unknown or legacy attestation kinds at policy load; fail closed if a declared entry or launcher artifact changes size during resolution.
non_goals: attesting a process whose executable or transitive dependencies changed after measurement
identity attestation without an explicit invocation snapshot
imprecise or non-injective artifact identity encoding
attesting a server name without binding to the measured process snapshot
trusting MCP-declared server metadata as identity proof

attack_classes.expected: missing, unsupported, mismatched, stale, or mixed-generation identity attestation denies tools/call with zero relay and never reports server_attested=true
